newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican business group sees job recovery next year.
newsitem.headline: Mexican business group sees job recovery next year.

text.p: Mexico will not begin to recover jobs lost in the wake of the December 1994 peso devaluation until next year, the Small Business Institute said on Tuesday.
"Employment is growing very slowly in Mexico," said Jorge Kawashi, president of the trade association, at a news conference.

"Growth in the informal economy is the best indication that the economy has yet to move into positive territory and allow lost jobs to be recovered," he said, adding that the economy should begin to recover its earlier employment levels next year.
Kawashi said rates of job creation would need to average 3.9 percent in each of the next few years to keep pace with new entrants to the labor force.
-- Maria Luisa Aguilar, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9553
